parent_platform_note: E2_on_E1 is most plausibly the 2026/09/13 20:51:33 submission scored 76.05 per the leaderboard report, but the link is not yet confirmed by submission ID.
single_hypothesis: Removing non-constant 64-bit division/modulo and repeated per-DMA alignment recomputation from the kernel hot path (by passing host-derived tilesPerRow/taskCount and using a general single-tile-per-row fast path) reduces Scalar work and lowers small-workload point latency without changing DMA structure, events, or numerics.
changed_mechanism: MhcExpandTilingData gains tilesPerRow (u32) and taskCount (u64), both already computed by Host; kernel stops recomputing them with 64-bit divisions

Kernel adds a general fast path for tilesPerRow==1 (equivalent to D<=tileLength, covers all D<=8192; not a shape whitelist) that replaces per-task task/tilesPerRow division and modulo with one multiply; D>8192 keeps the original general path

When the fast path applies and D is 16-element aligned with uint16-representable replica gaps, aligned DataCopyParams (blockLen/gaps) are precomputed once in Init and reused by every DMA, removing per-call CanUseAlignedCopy recomputation
FP16 backward skips InitBuffer for valueFp32Buf_ via if constexpr (unused since E2 Axpy); BF16 keeps it
unchanged_mechanisms: E2 FP16 backward mixed Axpy arithmetic and replica order
forward single-pass / ping-pong task split and ping-pong event protocol
backward TQue depth and vector barrier placement
DMA call counts, offsets, padding strategy, tail handling
domain_predicate: all supported FP16/BF16 forward and backward inputs; fast path activates for D<=tileLength (D<=8192) and degrades to the original general path otherwise
expected_risk: Tiling struct ABI grows 40->48 bytes (host and kernel compile together); simulator fixtures must add the two new fields; DataCopyParams precompute must exactly reproduce the old aligned-branch parameters

iterations.v1: used a TaskView struct returned by DecodeTask; forward small regressed +26 instruction calls from struct stack traffic; rebuilt with plain in-loop locals
iterations.v2: REJECTED, never submitted: static audit found the uniform CopyRowsOut fast branch put fastOutGapBlocks_ in the srcStride slot instead of dstStride, which would write contiguous GM rows (output corruption) for aligned multi-row tiles. msprof config mode cannot catch this because it does not export output tensors.
iterations.v3_final: dst-gap fix applied; binary + install pass in mhc_expand_local_test/build_round2_e3_scalar_hoist_v3 (fresh dir; v1/v2 build dirs kept for traceability)

build.notes: opParaSize grew 48->56 with the 48-byte tiling struct; host and kernel compile together so ABI stays consistent.

validation.actual_kernel: 7 CA-simulator cases executed with 'All task success': FP16 fwd/bwd small, FP16 bwd m8, BF16 fwd/bwd small, plus new boundary cases FP16 fwd S3 D8208 M2 (tilesPerRow=2 generic path) and FP16 bwd S3 D17 M4 (single-tile fast path + DataCopyPad). Output tensors were NOT exported by msprof 8.5 config mode, so golden comparison relies on the static parameter-equivalence audit below.
validation.static_equivalence_audit: For tilesPerRow==1: rowStart=task*rowBlock, columnOffset=0, validLength=d, alignedLength=align16(d) reproduce the old arithmetic exactly because the old code divided by a runtime tilesPerRow that equals 1 whenever d<=tileLength. When uniformAligned_ holds (d%16==0, blockLen and replica gaps fit uint16), the precomputed DataCopyParams{rowCount, d/16, gap, 0} are field-identical to the ones CanUseAlignedCopy produced (forward-in gap 0, forward-out gap (m-1)*d/16, backward-in gap (m-1)*d/16, backward-out gap 0). Non-uniform and tilesPerRow>1 inputs keep the original code path verbatim.
validation.mskpp_attempt: mskpp python direct-launch channel was explored end-to-end: the REAL host tiling library ran (48-byte tiling, blockdim and key correct) but the camodel kernel launch hung >6 min in this environment and was abandoned; see simulator/run_mskpp_case.py and simulator/README_simulator.md.

simulator.tool: msprof op simulator (CA mode); requires LD_LIBRARY_PATH to include tools/simulator/Ascend910B1/lib and tools/msopt/lib64, otherwise it silently reports success without executing
simulator.interpretation: Backward (points likely including 5 and the large m=8 cases) executes 3.0-5.6% fewer instructions; FP16 backward also drops one InitBuffer. Forward small executes ~21 more scalar instructions (~0.02 us at 1 GHz scalar issue, noise-level for a ~3.9 us point); large forward is expected to net-save from per-DMA constant folding but that is not measurable with local cases. 910B scalar division is a hardware instruction, so the original division-elimination hypothesis contributes little; the gains come from removing per-DMA alignment recomputation and the FP32 staging buffer.
